chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj), from which Wadi al-Aqiq should one enter the state of Ihram? He said: 'From its beginning, and that is superior.'

key_terms.أَوَّلِهِ: Its beginning (referring to the start of the valley)
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْعَقِيقِ: Wadi al-Aqiq, a famous valley near Mecca

ai.seo_question: Where is the best place to enter Ihram in Wadi al-Aqiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the preferred Miqat for residents of Medina, identifying the beginning of Wadi al-Aqiq as the optimal point for entering Ihram. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *afdaliyyah* (superiority/preference) in ritual acts, distinguishing between the obligatory minimum and the most virtuous practice. It underscores the precision required in Hajj rituals, where the location of Ihram directly impacts the validity and spiritual merit of the pilgrimage.
